display.title: The King and the Shabbos Candles
display.summary_short: An angry king bans all candles after a fire, but when he is lost in a snowstorm on Friday night, the light of Shabbos candles leads him to safety.
display.summary_long: A story from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Long ago, before electric lights, a king finishes remodeling his costly study, and a fallen candlestick burns it to the ground. In his anger he forbids anyone in his city to use candles. For the Jews this means no Shabbos lights, so the rabbi gathers everyone in shul to say Tehillim and asks them to beautify the mitzvah of Shabbos candles, with every daughter old enough to understand lighting alongside her mother. That Friday afternoon the king is riding in the forest when a fierce snowstorm breaks out. His frightened horse throws him and runs off, and the king crawls through the snow, lost and calling for help, until he sees a twinkling light far away: Shabbos candles in a cabin outside the city. He is given a royal welcome at a Shabbos table with white cloth, wine and challah, and he cancels his decree, saying his life was saved by a Shabbos candle.
display.lesson: The mitzvah of Shabbos candles brings light and protection; when we strengthen a mitzvah, Hashem answers our prayers.
